content: The Center for Scientific Review (CSR) serves as the primary gateway for grant applications submitted to the United States National Institutes of Health (NIH). It is responsible for organizing the peer review groups, also known as study sections, that assess the scientific merit of approximately 70% of the research grant applications submitted to the NIH. Additionally, the CSR processes all grant applications for the NIH and certain other divisions within the United States Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS). Since its establishment in 1946, the CSR has maintained a clear and essential mission: This process enables the NIH to allocate funding to the most promising research proposals. Each year, the CSR receives nearly 80,000 grant applications and enlists the expertise of over 18,000 external reviewers to evaluate these submissions within its study sections. These study sections typically convene three times annually. Beyond this, additional scientists contribute to NIH advisory councils, which provide a secondary level of peer review. These councils make funding recommendations based on priorities established by the United States Congress, the DHHS, and public interests. The CSR is currently pursuing several initiatives to enhance the grant review process. These include: 1. Shortening the Review Process: Efforts are underway to reduce the duration of the review process by 45 days. This adjustment would allow applicants to revise and resubmit their applications within the next review cycle, potentially reducing the resubmission timeline by four months. This change aims to expedite the funding of high-quality research. 2. Recruiting and Retaining Top Reviewers: 3. Encouraging Innovation: The CSR seeks to foster a review culture that is more supportive of innovative research proposals.
